$comment: Maps every top-level section of the PRE-REFACTOR root CLAUDE.md (2,256 lines, git rev at
'baseline' below) to where its content now lives. This file is the evidence for the claim
that the refactor relocated guidance rather than deleting it.
root                 -> stayed in root CLAUDE.md (safety-critical or universally true)
rule:<path>          -> a path-scoped rule under .claude/rules/ (loads on matching file)
nested:<path>        -> a nested CLAUDE.md (loads when a file in that tree is read)
skill:<name>         -> a skill under .claude/skills/ (loads on invocation)

budget.note: Anthropic guidance is ~200 lines per CLAUDE.md. Ceiling set slightly above the achieved result (190 lines) to allow small additions without churn. Raising it requires justifying why the content is unrecoverable-if-violated or true-on-every-task.

$comment: Broken links and dead heading-anchors that predate the CLAUDE.md refactor and sit outside
its blast radius (rot in guides/, mostly pointing at plans/ files deleted some time ago).
This is a ratchet, not an amnesty. Each entry is recorded so the debt is visible rather than
hidden, and ANY new broken reference fails the gate. Delete entries as they are fixed --
the checker does not require an entry to still be broken, so a stale entry is harmless.
Do not add to this list to silence a reference YOU broke. Fix it.

$notes.plans/MEMORY_LEAK_AUDIT.md -> ../../../C: Kept rather than repointed because there is no correct target. The path escapes the repo root AND '#memory-leaks' was never a heading in root at any revision -- no instruction file documents listener-leak antipatterns. Repointing it would produce a link that resolves but does not contain what the sentence claims, which is worse than a visibly broken one. Fixing this means either writing that guidance or dropping the claim, and both are edits to an unrelated audit document.
$notes.removed-by-slug-fix: Three anchor entries were dropped from this list because they were never really broken -- the checker's slugifier trimmed the leading/trailing hyphen that GitHub keeps when it strips an emoji from a heading, so it falsely reported dead anchors against this repo's 34 emoji-prefixed headings. The slugifier now matches GitHub and those three validate.
$notes.depth-errors-fixed: Ten pre-existing links in plans/ pointed at instruction files with the wrong number of '../' segments. They were fixed rather than grandfathered: each had one unambiguous intended target that exists, so the fix is a one-token change, and starting the inbound-refs category with ten grandfathered entries would bury exactly the signal that check exists to produce.
